objective.text: Distinguish migration rollback from restoration of data destroyed by a migration.

difficulty.rationale: Separate recreating a schema shape from restoring data that was removed.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A migration drops an obsolete notes column. Its down method adds an empty nullable notes column again. Does migrate:rollback restore the old note text?

options.text: No; recreating the column does not restore its deleted values.
options.rationale: The down method reverses the schema operation as written; recovery of removed data needs a preserved copy or another explicit data-restoration procedure.

options.text: Only if the command is run with --force, because that enables value restoration.
options.rationale: The force option bypasses an environment confirmation; it is not a backup-recovery mechanism.
options.misconception: The force option bypasses an environment confirmation; it is not a backup-recovery mechanism.

options.text: Yes; adding the same column name makes the database reconstruct its prior contents.
options.rationale: Reusing a name does not recreate discarded row values.
options.misconception: Reusing a name does not recreate discarded row values.

options.text: Yes; Laravel stores every dropped column’s values in the migrations table.
options.rationale: The migration repository records migration execution, not automatic snapshots of all affected data.
options.misconception: The migration repository records migration execution, not automatic snapshots of all affected data.
